recruit_text.backstory: Elie drew blood for a living at a clinic in Achrafieh, and he was the one the nervous patients asked for. He arrived here with a tourniquet in his pocket and found out that blood listens to him now. He heals with it, which most bloodmages think is a waste and he thinks is the only sensible use. He's calm, warm and careful, and very hard to rattle.

stages.stranger: I'm Elie, and I'm a healer, of a sort. Give me your arm, habibi. I promise this is the least frightening thing you'll see down here.
stages.acquaintance: I'm from Beirut, from Achrafieh, near the sea. I drew blood at a clinic there for ten years, and I was the one the nervous patients asked for, because I talk the whole time and they forget to be scared. Every evening I rode an old motorbike along the Corniche at sunset. It ran on spare parts and prayers.
stages.companion: My father died when I was nine. My mother, Mireille, raised three of us on a seamstress's wage, and every Sunday she cooked for twenty. I was in the middle of a draw at the clinic when everything went, and I woke up in the dark under Khaz Varun with a tourniquet in my pocket and this blue cap clipped to my sleeve. It's from the last needle I used at home. I haven't found her, or my sisters.
stages.friend: I was saving for medical school in Montpellier. Six years of saving, and every time I nearly had enough, something happened. The crash, the port, my sister's wedding. Now I'm a healer anyway, without the school. The Ashclaim want me to teach six of their healers my way, and I said yes. But I need to see the sea first, habibi. I'm starting to forget what it sounds like. Will you take me?
stages.sworn: It wasn't the Mediterranean, and it was enough. I stood in the surf at the Tempest Shallows until it got dark, and it sounded like the Corniche, almost. I asked at every hub on the way back, and nobody had heard of my mother or my sisters. I don't know if Beirut crossed over, or the sea with it. I teach my six now, and on Sundays I cook for them, the way she did. You keep the needle cap. I don't need needles any more.

moments.prompt: Elie is holding out his hand for your arm.

options.reply: Look at the wall, not at me. There, it's done, and you didn't even notice.
Ça va, that's fine. I'll be right here when you change your mind.

moments.prompt: He's asked you to take him all the way to the coast.

options.text: Let's go and find you the sea.
options.reply: Yalla, habibi, let's go. I'll heal everyone we meet on the way. I can't help it.

options.text: Is the sea worth the danger?
options.reply: For me, yes. I can't teach six people to heal if I've forgotten what home sounds like.

lines.bored_warning: Habibi, nobody's bled in days. Lovely for them, but I'm bored out of my mind.
lines.leaving_good: Nobody needed me much, which is the best kind of trip for a healer. I'll be in the upper halls of Khaz Varun.
lines.leaving_bored: My trainees in Khaz Varun need me more than this does. Yalla, I'm going.
lines.after_wipe: Stay down, everyone, and breathe. I'll come to each of you, and it won't hurt.
lines.wipe_warning: I can patch you all up again, but I'd rather not have to. After this run, I'm resting in the halls.
lines.wipe_leave: Khalas, that's enough for me. I'll be in Khaz Varun, teaching people not to do what we just did.
lines.zone_warning: Habibi, I can't bring back blood that's already left the body, and this place would make me try.
lines.zone_leave: I won't be the healer at the back of that. Find me in the upper halls of Khaz Varun.
lines.gear_refuse: Not that one, habibi, sorry. Ask me when we've had a Sunday lunch together.
lines.gear_taken: Ça va, take it. I worked ten years with a needle and a smile.
lines.gear_short: I'm missing a piece of kit, habibi. I'll heal around it, but I'd rather not.
lines.gear_upgrade: Merci, habibi, that's beautiful. You've spoiled me.
lines.back: The halls are quiet and my trainees can manage a day. Give me your arm, and let's go.
lines.send_word: Elie has sent word from Khaz Varun. His trainees can spare him, and he's ready.
lines.walkout_talk: Habibi, that wasn't the way to leave, and I know it. Sit, give me your arm, and I'll explain while I check you.
lines.neglect: Ah, habibi, finally! I've been telling my trainees about you, and they think I made you up.
lines.asked_to_stay: Yalla, one more. My trainees will survive without me.
lines.on_break: Elie is back in the upper halls of Khaz Varun, training healers. Come back after you've done a few more jobs.

town_arrive.text: My mother cooked for twenty every Sunday, and if you were late you got the burnt bits. I was always late.

zone_arrive.text: Every new place, I listen for the sea first. Nothing yet, habibi.

close_call.text: Arm, please, quickly. There, you're fine, and you barely felt it.

dungeon_clear.text: Everyone's colour is good. I've been checking, don't worry.
